summary.en: Abdul El-Sayed, a former public health official, secured the Democratic nomination in Michigan's Senate race, defeating congresswoman Haley Stevens. He celebrated his victory as a triumph over significant external financial influence.

title.en: Ukraine pleads for interceptors after Russian missile attack kills at least 17
title.zh: 俄罗斯导弹袭击致至少17人死亡，乌克兰请求拦截器

summary.en: Russian missile attacks on Kyiv killed at least 17 people, prompting Ukraine to appeal for more interceptor systems. Ukraine's air force reported intercepting most drones but no missiles during the intensified assaults.
summary.zh: 俄罗斯对基辅的导弹袭击造成至少17人死亡，促使乌克兰呼吁提供更多拦截系统。乌克兰空军报告称，在这些加剧的袭击中，大部分无人机被拦截，但没有导弹被拦截。

body.en:
Russian missile and drone strikes killed at least 17 people and wounded dozens more in Kyiv and the surrounding region, as Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said interceptors "could have saved lives".

Ukraine was unable to shoot down any of the missiles launched by Russia, whose intensifying attacks have prompted Ukraine to plead for more United States-made Patriot interceptors.

Russia has significantly upped its attacks on the Ukrainian capital in recent months , typically firing salvos of hard-to-intercept ballistic missiles in short blitzes that rock buildings and send booms echoing across the city.

"Ballistic interceptors are what could have saved the lives of those killed today," Zelenskyy said on Wednesday.

Zelenskyy said he had been in talks with NATO chief Mark Rutte about getting interceptor missiles.

"It is important to cut through all red tape and make the necessary political decisions," he said on social media.

"Literally every day, people's lives here in Ukraine depend on the resolve of our partners in Europe and the United States."

A cloud of smoke hovered over the capital at sunrise, AFP journalists saw, after the attacks sparked fires in several locations in the region.

More than 40 people were wounded in the capital and its surrounding areas, local authorities said.

AFP journalists heard explosions in Kyiv after midnight (7am Wednesday AEST), following Ukrainian air force warnings of incoming ballistic missiles.

One journalist reported seeing dark smoke and the acrid smell of burning lingering in the air hours later.

"The night was so terrifying, so hard," Kyiv resident Natalia Reutska told AFP in the morning after the attack.

"We've gotten used to waking up thinking, 'we were lucky today,' and that's very scary," she added.

Ukraine shot down 98 of the 115 drones fired by Russia overnight, the air force said.

But it was unable to shoot down any of the missiles, preliminary statistics from the air force showed.

EU chief Ursula von der Leyen slammed "horrible atrocities". French President Emmanuel Macron called for heavier sanctions against Russia.

Ukraine can intercept the vast majority of drones, but still relies on supplies from allies to counter missiles.

Zelenskyy said the number of air-defence missiles supplied from allies had dropped threefold compared with 2025.

He has repeatedly warned about critical air-defence shortages, as Russia fired a record number of missiles at Ukraine in July, an AFP analysis of Ukrainian air force data published Saturday showed.

reflection.en: In the face of relentless attacks and profound loss, communities endure immense suffering. Yet, even amidst devastation, the steadfast love and mercies of Yahweh are new every morning, offering a source of enduring hope and strength.
reflection.zh: 面对无情的袭击和深重的损失，社区承受着巨大的痛苦。然而，即使在毁灭之中，雅伟的坚定慈爱和怜悯每天早晨都是新的，为人们提供了持久的希望和力量。

verse.textEn: Because of Yahweh's great love we are not consumed, for his compassions never fail. They are new every morning.

title.en: Senate confirms Trump pick Erica Schwartz as new CDC director
title.zh: 参议院确认特朗普提名的埃丽卡·施瓦茨为疾控中心新主任

summary.en: The US Senate confirmed Dr. Erica Schwartz as the new director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) in a 51-44 vote, marking a successful appointment for the Trump administration.
summary.zh: 美国参议院以51票对44票确认埃丽卡·施瓦茨博士为疾病控制与预防中心（CDC）新任主任，这标志着特朗普政府的一次成功任命。

body.en: Schwartz, president’s third pick to lead top US public health agency, confirmed in 51-44 Senate vote Dr Erica Schwartz was confirmed by the US Senate as director ‌of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), a rare win for the Trump administration after a string of failed attempts to fill senior health posts. Schwartz was confirmed by a ⁠51-44 vote that broke largely along party lines, with Tim Kaine of Virginia the sole Democrat to support her nomination. Continue reading...
body.zh: 施瓦茨是总统第三位领导美国最高公共卫生机构的人选，在参议院以 51 比 44 的投票结果确认埃里卡·施瓦茨博士被美国参议院确认为疾病控制与预防中心 (CDC) 主任，这是特朗普政府在一系列填补高级卫生职位失败的尝试后罕见的胜利。施瓦茨以 51 比 44 的投票结果获得确认，该投票很大程度上打破了党派界限，弗吉尼亚州的蒂姆·凯恩 (Tim Kaine) 是唯一支持她提名的民主党人。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The confirmation of a new director for a vital public health agency underscores the importance of wise leadership and expert counsel for a nation's well-being. In times of complex challenges, the collective wisdom of many can guide us toward safety and stability, reflecting Yahweh's provision for governance.
reflection.zh: 确认一位重要公共卫生机构的新主任，突显了明智的领导和专家建议对国家福祉的重要性。在面临复杂挑战时，众多的智慧能指引我们走向安全和稳定，这反映了雅伟对治理的供应。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Judge tosses Alex Murdaugh’s $600,000 suit against former court clerk
title.zh: 法官驳回亚历克斯·默多夫对前法院书记员提起的60万美元诉讼

summary.en: A US federal judge has dismissed a $600,000 lawsuit filed by Alex Murdaugh against a former court clerk. Murdaugh's murder convictions were previously overturned due to the clerk's misconduct, and he is now set to face trial again.
summary.zh: 一名美国联邦法官驳回了亚历克斯·默多夫对一名前法院书记员提起的60万美元诉讼。默多夫的谋杀罪名此前因该书记员的不当行为而被推翻，他现在将再次面临审判。

body.en: Murdaugh, whose murder convictions were overturned due to clerk’s misconduct, will face trial again Sign up for the Breaking News US newsletter email A US federal judge has thrown out a lawsuit by Alex Murdaugh seeking $600,000 in legal fees from the former court clerk whose misconduct led to his murder convictions being overturned on appeal. Murdaugh sued Becky Hill in May, saying she violated his right to a fair trial over the deaths of his wife and son. Continue reading...
body.zh: 由于书记员不当行为，默多的谋杀定罪被推翻，他将再次面临审判 美国联邦法官驳回了亚历克斯·默多向这位前法院书记员索要 60 万美元律师费的诉讼，默多的不当行为导致他的谋杀定罪在上诉中被推翻。默多于五月起诉贝基·希尔，称她侵犯了他因妻子和儿子的死亡而受到公平审判的权利。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story reminds us that integrity in seemingly small roles can have profound consequences, impacting the course of justice and individual lives. Yahweh's word teaches that faithfulness in little things reflects a deeper character, essential for trust and accountability in any system.
reflection.zh: 这个故事提醒我们，在看似微小的岗位上保持正直，也可能产生深远的影响，左右着司法进程和个人命运。雅伟的话语教导我们，在小事上忠心反映出更深层的品格，这对于任何系统中的信任和问责都至关重要。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Republican who withdrew last month beats Trump-backed rival in Michigan
title.zh: 上月退选的共和党人击败特朗普支持的对手，赢得密歇根州初选

summary.en: Thomas Smith, a Republican candidate who withdrew from the primary contest for Michigan’s eighth district last month, unexpectedly won the nomination on Tuesday, with his name remaining on the ballot.
summary.zh: 共和党候选人托马斯·史密斯上月退出了密歇根州第八选区的初选，但由于他的名字仍在选票上，他于周二意外赢得了提名。

body.en: Thomas Smith, whose name remained on ballot, beats Republican rivals in primary contest for eighth district Thomas Smith withdrew from the Republican primary contest for Michigan’s eighth district last month. On Tuesday, he won the nomination. Unofficial results show Smith with more than 50% of the vote, according to the Associated Press, defeating the man he endorsed, anti-abortion activist Al Lemmo, and the man Donald Trump endorsed, former federal law enforcement officer Amir Hassan. Continue reading...

reflection.en: The unexpected victory of a candidate who had withdrawn from the race highlights how human plans and endorsements do not always dictate outcomes. This reminds us that ultimate authority and the power to elevate or humble leaders rest with Yahweh.
reflection.zh: 一位已退选的候选人意外获胜，这表明人类的计划和支持并不总是决定结果。这提醒我们，最终的权柄以及提升或贬低领袖的能力，都掌握在雅伟手中。

verse.textEn: It is God who judges: He brings one down, he exalts another.
verse.textZh: 惟有神断定；他使这人降卑，使那人升高。

title.en: Cambridge professor Jason Arday resigns amid accusations of plagiarism

Arday, who had been dogged by a growing series of questions over his academic work and credentials, issued a statement on Wednesday night, saying the “relentless accusations, speculation and public commentary have taken a profound toll on me and on those I love”. reflection.en: The news of a prominent academic's resignation due to accusations of plagiarism reminds us that integrity is paramount, especially in positions of influence. reflection.zh: 一位知名学者因抄袭指控而辞职的消息提醒我们，诚信至关重要，尤其是在有影响力的人士身上。雅伟的话语警告说，骄傲往往在跌倒之前，这突显了在我们所有的努力中谦逊和诚实的重要性。

verse.textEn: Pride goes before destruction, a haughty spirit before a fall.
verse.textZh: 骄傲在败坏以先；狂心在跌倒之前。

title.en: Israel strikes south Lebanon after first evacuation warning in weeks
title.zh: 以色列在数周来首次疏散警告后袭击黎巴嫩南部

summary.en: Lebanon's health ministry reported one fatality from Israeli strikes in south Lebanon. The Israeli military stated these strikes were a response to a ceasefire violation by Hezbollah.
summary.zh: 黎巴嫩卫生部报告称，以色列对黎巴嫩南部发动的袭击造成一人死亡。以色列军方表示，这些袭击是对真主党违反停火协议的回应。

body.en:
One person has been killed in an Israeli strike in southern Lebanon, the country's health ministry says, after the Israeli military said it was responding to a "blatant violation of the ceasefire" by the Iran-backed group Hezbollah.

A man died and 12 other people were injured when the roof of a prayer hall at the cemetery of the town of Tibnin was hit, according to Lebanese media.

Strikes were also reported to the west in the town of Mansouri, where the Israeli military issued its first evacuation order for more than a month.

Hezbollah has not commented on the events, which came as Israeli and Lebanese officials attended US-sponsored talks in Rome aimed at maintaining the ceasefire.

In late June, the three countries agreed a trilateral framework that should see the Israeli military gradually withdraw from territory it is occupying in southern Lebanon in exchange for the disarmament of Hezbollah.

Two weeks ago, the Lebanese army was allowed to deploy to one of the first "pilot zones", after Israeli troops pulled out of the village of Zawtar al-Gharbiyeh.

Hezbollah has rejected the agreement, saying the provisions linking Israel's withdrawal to the group's disarmament crossed "all red lines".

The Israeli military announced that it had begun carrying out "precise strikes" in southern Lebanon on Wednesday afternoon, about 30 minutes after its Arabic spokesperson had told residents of Mansouri to evacuate ahead of "forceful action" there.

Both statements accused Hezbollah of violating the ceasefire but gave no further details.

However, an Israeli military source told Israeli media that displaced residents of Mansouri had returned to their town "under the auspices of the Lebanese army, which established a checkpoint in the area in violation of the agreements".

The source said the town was inside the Israeli-declared "security zone" - a 10km (six-mile) deep strip of occupied Lebanese territory running along the border - and "military activity that endangers the lives of Lebanese civilians" was taking place there.

The evacuation order was the first issued in southern Lebanon since 14 June, when residents of 29 towns and villages were told to flee their homes.

Earlier on Wednesday, the mayor of Mansouri, Haidar Madihli, told local media that Israeli warplanes had carried out four strikes on buildings and villas in the Ghazaleh neighbourhood on the outskirts of the town, causing extensive damage to the targeted structures.

The strikes triggered a wave of displacement, with families filling cars with their belongings and heading towards Tyre, the largest city in the south, Madihli said.

title.en: Drone carrying explosives found at German airport, police say
title.zh: 警方称德国机场发现携带爆炸物的无人机

summary.en: The drone was found near Ukrainian cargo planes before another object collided with a cargo aircraft in mid-air.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A drone carrying an explosive device has been found at a German airport, police say.

A robot was deployed at Leipzig/Halle Airport after the device was spotted by an employee near Ukrainian cargo planes overnight, according to Saxony police. A second unidentified object also collided with a cargo aircraft near the same airport. It landed in Hanover with minor damage.

German airports are on high alert following several unauthorised drone flights in recent months over military bases, airports, energy terminals, seaports and logistics companies. Police have warned of a potential Russian involvement which Moscow has denied.

Leipzig/Halle Airport in eastern Germany is used by the Germany military and Nato allies for the transport of military goods and also serves as a base for Ukraine's Antonov Airlines - which carry most of the country's aerial cargo.

A police spokesman told the BBC that the explosive-laden object had been spotted close to parked Antonov planes.

The detonator was removed from the explosive device. Police later carried out a controlled explosion. Flights on the northern runway resumed at 01:55 (23:55 GMT on Tuesday). The southern runway remains closed.

"All of this does not point to an amateurish approach. We are talking about a professional, hybrid threat scenario that we will continue to address," German Interior Minister Alexander Dobrindt said.

He did not name any suspects, but suggested the investigation may point to a possible "competition" that "may also involve foreign powers".

Ukraine's Ambassador to Germany Oleksii Makeiev told Welt TV: "Who else could it be but Russia?"

Similar incidents with suspicious drones in Germany have only happened since Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, Peter R Neumann, a professor of Security Studies at King's College London, said on X.

"Since last night, the drone war has reached Germany. And it exposes a weakness that we've known about for years," he said.

In July 2024 a parcel burst into flames on the ground at Leipzig/Halle Airport before it could be loaded onto a DHL cargo plane, one of a series of parcel fires that targeted the UK and EU countries.

The parcels had contained explosive devices that were set off by electronic timers hidden in vibrating massage pillows, according to authorities.

Last year a Chinese woman was convicted for passing on information about flight schedules and cargo movements at Leipzig/Halle Airport to a man spying for Beijing.
body.zh: 警方称，在德国机场发现了一架携带爆炸装置的无人机。 据萨克森警方称，一名员工夜间在乌克兰货机附近发现了该设备，随后莱比锡/哈勒机场部署了一个机器人。第二个不明物体还与同一机场附近的一架货机相撞。它降落在汉诺威，受到轻微损坏。 近几个月来，在军事基地、机场、能源码头、海港和物流公司上空发生了数起未经授权的无人机飞行事件，德国机场处于高度戒备状态。警方警告称，俄罗斯可能参与其中，但莫斯科方面予以否认。 德国东部的莱比锡/哈勒机场被德国军方和北约盟国用来运输军用物资，也是乌克兰安东诺夫航空公司的基地，该航空公司运输该国大部分航空货物。 警方发言人告诉英国广播公司，在停放的安东诺夫飞机附近发现了这个充满爆炸物的物体。 雷管已从爆炸装置中取出。警方随后进行了受控爆炸。北部跑道的航班于 01:55（周二 23:55 GMT）恢复。南部跑道仍然关闭。 德国内政部长亚历山大·多布林特 (Alexander Dobrindt) 表示：“所有这一切并不意味着采取业余方法。我们正在谈论一种专业的、混合的威胁场景，我们将继续解决这一问题。” 他没有透露任何嫌疑人的名字，但表示调查可能表明可能存在“竞争”，“也可能涉及外国势力”。 乌克兰驻德国大使奥列克西·马基耶夫（Oleksii Makeiev）告诉世界电视台：“除了俄罗斯还能是谁？” 伦敦国王学院安全研究教授彼得·R·诺伊曼 (Peter R Neumann) 表示，自 2022 年 2 月俄罗斯全面入侵乌克兰以来，德国才发生过类似的可疑无人机事件。 “从昨晚开始，无人机战争已经波及德国。它暴露了我们多年来已知的弱点，”他说。 2024 年 7 月，莱比锡/哈勒机场的一个包裹在被装上 DHL 货机之前在地面上起火，这是针对英国和欧盟国家的一系列包裹火灾之一。 据当局称，这些包裹中含有爆炸装置，这些爆炸装置是由隐藏在振动按摩枕头中的电子计时器引发的。 去年，一名中国女子因向一名为北京从事间谍活动的男子传递有关莱比锡/哈勒机场航班时刻表和货物运输的信息而被定罪。

summary.en: Russia is preparing a new mobilization campaign to boost troop numbers, Ukrainian officials and independent Russian media outlets report. The Kremlin denies this.

Russia is preparing a new mobilization campaign to boost troop numbers, Ukrainian officials and independent Russian media outlets report. The Kremlin denies this.

Russian authorities are planning to "expand mobilization" in autumn this year, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has said, citing intelligence services. According to Zelenskyy, Russian President Vladimir Putin is reportedly preparing to recruit additional Russian soldiers to fight in the war against Ukraine .

"He is concealing his intention behind different words and signals, but he is making preparations," Zelenskyy said. "It is important that we, together with our partners, exert sufficient pressure on Russia so that the idea of ending this aggression — the idea of peace, rather than further Russian mobilization — prevails," he added. The Ukrainian president also said Russia's army was losing more fighters at the front than it can recruit, even though Putin wants to intensify the attacks and expand the war.

Putin issued a decree in autumn 2022 launching a "partial mobilization," which remains in effect to this day, as confirmed by the presidential administration in 2023. The document, it said, "regulates additional measures necessary to ensure that the armed forces fulfill their objectives."

Independent Russian exile media outlet Verstka and Latvia-based Russian-language news portal Vaschnyje Istorii published an investigative report in late June stating that Russia's leadership was secretly "discussing mobilization" given the difficulties in recruiting new conscripts. One source quoted by Verstka said figures by Moscow ' s mayoral office show the city sent 1,708 people to the front in April of this year and 1,378 in May — around 1,000 fewer people than during the same period last year. This low recruitment rate reportedly continued in June as well.

Vaschnyje Istorii reported that the recruitment rate for soldiers serving on fixed-term contracts more than halved in the last quarter of 2025 compared with the same period the previous year. The outlet said the recruitment rate had dropped even further in early 2026. The news outlet also cited sources from different Russian regions revealing that the number of people applying for army contracts was falling.

Military personnel interviewed by Verstka said that contract soldiers being sent to fight this year were "unfit for combat," with many new arrivals fleeing the front lines. One conscript told the news outlet that "units are staffed at 30 to 40%, at best."

title.en: Watch: 'Scariest night' as Ukraine fails to intercept Russian attack
title.zh: 观看：乌克兰未能拦截俄罗斯袭击，度过“最可怕的夜晚”

summary.en: Kyiv's depleted air defences meant many of the missiles were not intercepted - like the one that hit Anastasiia's home.
summary.zh: 基辅防空力量耗尽，导致许多导弹未能被拦截——其中一枚击中了阿纳斯塔西娅的家。

body.en:
Twenty-one people were killed and dozens have been injured after Russia fired 115 drones and 24 ballistic missiles in Ukraine.

Many of the drones were intercepted, but Kyiv's depleted air defences meant many of the missiles were not.

Anastasiia Dudley's home was significantly damaged in the attack, which she said was the "scariest night" of the war.

The BBC's Dan Johnson visited Anastasiia's home near Kyiv to see the extent of the damage and the emotional toll on residents.
body.zh: 俄罗斯向乌克兰发射了115架无人机和24枚弹道导弹，造成21人死亡、数十人受伤。 许多无人机被拦截，但基辅的防空系统已被耗尽，这意味着许多导弹没有被拦截。 阿纳斯塔西娅·达德利 (Anastasiia Dudley) 的家在袭击中严重受损，她说这是战争中“最可怕的夜晚”。 英国广播公司 (BBC) 的丹·约翰逊 (Dan Johnson) 访问了阿纳斯塔西娅 (Anastasiia) 在基辅附近的家，了解受损程度以及居民的情感损失。

reflection.en: The "scariest night" described in Kyiv reminds us of the profound vulnerability when homes and lives are directly threatened by conflict. In such moments of overwhelming trouble, we are reminded that Yahweh remains our refuge and strength, an ever-present help. Even when human defenses falter, there is a steadfast hope in divine presence.
reflection.zh: 基辅所描述的“最可怕的夜晚”提醒我们，当家园和生命受到冲突直接威胁时，人类是多么脆弱。在这样压倒性的困境中，我们被提醒雅伟仍是我们的避难所和力量，是患难中随时的帮助。即使人类的防御失效，在神的同在中仍有坚定的盼望。

summary.en: The "cockroach" movement was one of the biggest public displays of dissent against India's prime minister in years.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The recent youth-led protests have weakened Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi "terribly", says leading activist Sonam Wangchuk whose hunger strike galvanised the movement.

Wangchuk told the BBC that the atmosphere in the country had changed following mass demonstrations which triggered the resignation of the education minister on 25 July.

Young people now have more confidence they can "change things if they want to" and feel they don't have to "take everything lying down", the 59-year-old said.

The "cockroach" movement mounted one of the biggest public displays of dissent against Modi's government, which has been in power since 2014.

The movement takes its name from a remark by India's chief justice, who drew criticism after comparing sections of unemployed young people to "cockroaches" during a court hearing.

Wangchuk fasted in scorching heat in the capital, Delhi, for 26 days in June and July, consuming only salt and water. He says he has now regained six of the 11kg he lost.

The activist was forcibly taken to hospitals which he says were "more like prisons" for the final six days of his fast.

By then, the protests had escalated from public anger about the leak of exam papers into some of the biggest anti-government demonstrations India had seen in years.

Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned the day after Wangchuk ended his hunger strike.

Since then, Modi has announced fast-track courts to try those accused in the leaks and appointed a tech billionaire to lead efforts to reform the examination system.

The government also said it would offer compensation to families of students who took their own lives after exam questions were leaked.

But India's problems are deeper - with graduate unemployment hovering around 35-40% for the past 25 years.

The engineer and education specialist says exams currently have little relevance to the job market.

Often based on multiple-choice questions, they are designed to assess millions of students efficiently, with no consideration of how effectively they measure skills and understanding, he says. This, in turn, shapes how schools teach.

If exams placed greater emphasis on hands-on experience and aptitude, he suggests, schools might adapt their methods and help address India's jobs crisis.

"There needs to be some planning of what the world and the country are likely to look like in 15 years," Wangchuk says.

Changing the way children are taught might help ensure they are "not left unemployed and sectors that need people are not left underemployed".

India's government has previously defended itself against criticism of its handling of the economy. It argues that claims of an unemployment crisis are overstated and that its macroeconomic policy remains fundamentally robust.

body.zh: 活动家索南·旺楚克 (Sonam Wangchuk) 表示，最近由年轻人领导的抗议活动“严重”削弱了印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪的实力。索南·旺楚克的绝食活动激发了这场运动。 旺楚克告诉 BBC，大规模示威导致教育部长于 7 月 25 日辞职，该国的气氛发生了变化。 这位 59 岁的年轻人现在更有信心，他们可以“如果愿意的话可以改变事情”，并且觉得自己不必“放下一切”。 “蟑螂”运动是对莫迪政府自 2014 年执政以来最大规模的公开异议之一。 该运动得名于印度首席大法官的一句话，他在法庭听证会上将部分失业年轻人比作“蟑螂”后招致批评。 6月和7月，旺楚克在首都德里的酷暑中禁食了26天，只吃盐和水。他说他现在已经减掉了 11 公斤，其中 6 公斤又回来了。 这位活动人士被强行送往医院，他说在禁食的最后六天，医院“更像是监狱”。 那时，抗议活动已经从公众对试卷泄露的愤怒升级为印度多年来最大规模的反政府示威活动。 旺楚克结束绝食后第二天，教育部长达门德拉·普拉丹(Dharmendra Pradhan)辞职。 此后，莫迪宣布设立快速法庭来审判那些被指控泄密的人，并任命了一位科技亿万富翁来领导考试制度的改革工作。 政府还表示，将向考试题目泄露后自杀的学生家属提供赔偿。 但印度的问题更为严重——过去 25 年毕业生失业率一直徘徊在 35-40% 左右。 这位工程师兼教育专家表示，目前的考试与就业市场关系不大。 他说，它们通常基于多项选择题，旨在有效地评估数百万学生，而不考虑它们衡量技能和理解力的有效性。这反过来又决定了学校的教学方式。 他建议，如果考试更加注重实践经验和能力，学校可能会调整方法，帮助解决印度的就业危机。 旺楚克说：“需要对 15 年后世界和国家的面貌进行一些规划。” 改变儿童的教育方式可能有助于确保他们“不会失业，需要人才的部门不会失业”。 印度政府此前曾针对对其经济处理方式的批评进行了辩护。它认为，有关失业危机的说法被夸大了，其宏观经济政策从根本上来说仍然强劲。 与此同时，报道...

title.en: India's Gen Z protest enters a new online battle
title.zh: 印度Z世代抗议进入新的线上战场

summary.en: India's Generation Z is engaging in a new form of protest, moving from street demonstrations to an online battle. The fight over the legacy of the Cockroach Janta Party movement is now intensifying across platforms like Instagram and through the use of memes and other social media content.
summary.zh: 印度Z世代的抗议活动进入了新的线上战场。关于“蟑螂人民党”运动遗产的争论正在Instagram、表情包和社交媒体上日益激烈。

body.en:
The streets are quiet, but a fight over the legacy of the Cockroach Janta Party movement is intensifying across Instagram, memes and social media.

The crowds have long dispersed from the Cockroach Janta Party's (CJP) main New Delhi protest site next to the Jantar Mantar.

But the CJP's 36-day campaign, which started as a satirical protest against exam leaks and grew into a wider movement voicing young Indians' anger over jobs and education, has entered a new phase.

The authorities and the CJP are now battling to shape how India's first Gen Z-led protest will be remembered.

Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan resigned on July 25, fulfilling one of the CJP's key demands after weeks of protests that withstood tear gas and baton charges.

India's ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) says the minister's resignation demonstrates government accountability, while the CJP argues it was a concession won through sustained public pressure.

The BJP has mounted a coordinated online campaign aimed at reframing the movement, observers say.

MPs Bansuri Swaraj and Sambit Patra have shared videos of protesters allegedly abusing Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi and his late mother, while Modi himself said he forgave those responsible .

Meanwhile, BJP leaders J P Nadda and Pradhan have argued that opposition parties and "anti-national forces" sought to exploit genuine student grievances for political gain.

BJP spokesperson Shazia Ilmi rejects suggestions that the party is trying to divert attention from education reform .

"A generation capable of reinventing political communication through memes and satire should not have fallen back on crude abuse," Ilmi told DW, referring to slogans directed at Modi and his late mother.

Instead of lengthy political rebuttals, they have continued to flood Instagram with memes, parody reels and remix videos that mock the BJP's attempts to appear youthful, while insisting the central issue remains education reform and accountability. 

Apar Gupta, founding director of the Internet Freedom Foundation, believes the Cockroach movement exposed a generational shift in political communication.

"Instagram is a different ecosystem," he told DW. "It rewards authenticity, personal storytelling and virality, allowing Gen Z creators to set the terms of debate before official narratives can catch up."

"Gen Z may have won the cultural conversation through reels, memes and satire, but the state still retains institutional power through takedown requests, digital surveillance and investigations," Gupta said.

"The battle is no longer just over public opinion; it is over how the protests will be remembered."

body.zh: 街道上很安静，但 Instagram、表情包和社交媒体上围绕蟑螂简塔党运动遗产的斗争正在加剧。 蟑螂简塔党（CJP）新德里主要抗议地点靠近简塔·曼塔天文台的人群早已散去。 但 CJP 为期 36 天的运动已经进入了一个新阶段，该运动最初是对考试泄密的讽刺抗议，后来发展成为一场更广泛的运动，表达了印度年轻人对就业和教育的愤怒。 当局和印度人民党目前正在努力塑造如何纪念印度首次由 Z 世代领导的抗议活动。 教育部长达门德拉·普拉丹 (Dharmendra Pradhan) 于 7 月 25 日辞职，满足了 CJP 在抵抗催泪瓦斯和警棍指控的抗议活动数周后的一项关键要求。 印度执政党印度人民党（BJP）表示，部长的辞职表明了政府的责任，而印度人民党则认为这是通过持续的公众压力赢得的让步。 观察人士称，印度人民党发起了一场协调一致的在线运动，旨在重塑这场运动。 国会议员班苏里·斯瓦拉吉（Bansuri Swaraj）和桑比特·帕特拉（Sambit Patra）分享了抗议者据称辱骂印度总理纳伦德拉·莫迪及其已故母亲的视频，而莫迪本人则表示，他原谅了那些肇事者。 与此同时，印度人民党领导人 J P Nadda 和 Pradhan 认为，反对党和“反国家势力”试图利用学生的真正不满来获取政治利益。 印度人民党发言人沙齐亚·伊尔米（Shazia Ilmi）否认该党试图转移人们对教育改革注意力的说法。 伊尔米对德国之声表示：“能够通过迷因和讽刺重塑政治沟通的一代人不应该陷入粗暴的虐待之中。”他指的是针对莫迪及其已故母亲的口号。 他们没有进行冗长的政治反驳，而是继续在 Instagram 上发布大量表情包、恶搞视频和混音视频，嘲笑印度人民党试图显得年轻的做法，同时坚称核心问题仍然是教育改革和问责制。 互联网自由基金会的创始董事阿帕·古普塔认为，蟑螂运动暴露了政治传播的代际转变。 “Instagram 是一个不同的生态系统，”他告诉德国之声。 “它奖励真实性、个人故事讲述和病毒式传播，让 Z 世代的创作者能够在官方叙述赶上之前设定辩论条款。” 古普塔说：“Z 世代可能通过视频、迷因和讽刺赢得了文化对话，但国家仍然通过删除请求、数字监控和调查保留了机构权力。” “这场斗争不再只是围绕公众舆论；而是围绕如何记住抗议活动。” CJP 的创作者经常将政府公告与失业统计数据、取消的考试和...

reflection.en: In the digital arena, where narratives are quickly shaped and contested, it is wise to approach information with discernment. Yahweh's wisdom reminds us that the first account often seems right until another perspective is carefully considered. This calls us to seek understanding from all sides when a movement's legacy is being debated online.
reflection.zh: 在数字领域，叙事迅速形成并受到挑战，以明辨的态度对待信息是明智的。雅伟的智慧提醒我们，先陈述案情的人似乎有理，直到另一方前来查问。这呼吁我们在一个运动的遗产在网上被辩论时，要从各方寻求理解。

verse.textEn: In a lawsuit the first to speak seems right, until someone comes forward and cross-examines.
verse.textZh: 先诉情由的，似乎有理；但邻舍来到，就察出实情。

title.en: Hiroshima survivors warn against Japan's rearmament
title.zh: 广岛幸存者警告日本不要重新武装

summary.en: On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists tell DW Japan's military buildup risks eroding its longstanding commitment to pacifism.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
On the anniversary of the atomic bombings, survivors and activists tell DW Japan's military buildup risks eroding its longstanding commitment to pacifism.

Japan on Thursday commemorates the 81st anniversary of the nuclear attack on  Hiroshima .

On August 6, 1945, the US dropped an atomic bomb on the Japanese city of Hiroshima during the last days of World War II , killing close to 80,000 people in the initial blast. Three days later, the US dropped a bomb over Nagasaki.

"Japan adopted a pacifist constitution in reflection on World War II," noted Masako Wada, assistant secretary general of  Nihon Hidankyo , or the Japan Confederation of A- and H-Bomb Sufferers' Organizations. 

Japan "earned the trust of the international community as a country that promised never to wage a war again," added Wada, who survived the Nagasaki bombing as a 1-year-old.

However, in recent years, Japan has increased defense spending, eased restrictions on weapons exports and expanded the role of its military, citing growing risks from China , North Korea and Russia .

"The current administration is destroying that [trust]," Wada told DW, referring to Japan's recent efforts to pivot away from decades of strict postwar pacifism.

"Japan's recent military buildup is no different from recreating the arms race that led the country toward World War II," said 84-year-old Masashi Ieshima, who survived the Hiroshima bombing at the age of 3.

Ieshima was playing in the entrance of his house, just 1.2 miles (2 km) from the hypocenter, when the blast shattered all the windows in the house, sending shards of glass into his mother.

Seventy years later, he underwent surgery for thyroid cancer, which was officially recognized as an atomic bomb-related illness. His father, who was also exposed to the Hiroshima atomic bombing, died of laryngeal cancer.

"It makes my blood boil to see Japan justify its military buildup and the easing of arms export restrictions over the possibility of a Taiwan conflict ," said Ieshima, who serves as the chairman of Toyukai, the Tokyo affiliate of Nihon Hidankyo.

"If Japan continues down this path, it could lead to war. And if another war breaks out, I believe it will be a nuclear war." 

The average age of Japan's atomic bomb survivors, known as "hibakusha," has reached almost 87. They face the urgent challenge of passing on their testimony and calls for peace to younger generations, including their children, grandchildren, and supporters.

Takako Nakamura, a second-generation atomic bomb survivor from Nagasaki, began working actively as a family testimony speaker in February 2026, following her career retirement.

body.zh: 在原子弹爆炸周年纪念日之际，幸存者和活动人士告诉德国之声，日本的军备建设有可能侵蚀其对和平主义的长期承诺。 日本周四纪念广岛核袭击 81 周年。 1945 年 8 月 6 日，美国在第二次世界大战的最后几天向日本广岛投下了一颗原子弹，在最初的爆炸中造成近 8 万人死亡。三天后，美国在长崎投下了一颗炸弹。 日本原子弹受害者组织联合会助理秘书长和田正子指出：“日本通过了一部和平主义宪法，以反思第二次世界大战。” 一岁时在长崎原子弹爆炸中幸存下来的和田补充道，日本“作为一个承诺不再发动战争的国家赢得了国际社会的信任”。 然而，近年来，日本以来自中国、朝鲜和俄罗斯的风险日益增加为由，增加了国防开支，放宽了对武器出口的限制，并扩大了军队的作用。 “现任政府正在摧毁这种[信任]，”和田告诉德国之声，他指的是日本最近努力摆脱几十年来严格的战后和平主义。 “日本最近的军备建设无异于重现导致该国走向第二次世界大战的军备竞赛，”3 岁时在广岛原子弹爆炸中幸存下来的 84 岁老人家岛雅志 (Masashi Ieshima) 说。 伊江岛正在自家门口玩耍，距离震源仅 1.2 英里（2 公里），爆炸震碎了房子里的所有窗户，玻璃碎片飞进了他的母亲体内。 七十年后，他接受了甲状腺癌手术，甲状腺癌被正式认定为与原子弹相关的疾病。他的父亲也曾遭受广岛原子弹爆炸，因喉癌去世。 担任日本飞段协东京分公司东友会董事长的家岛说：“看到日本证明其军事集结和放松武器出口限制是合理的，这让我热血沸腾。” “如果日本继续走这条路，可能会导致战争。如果另一场战争爆发，我相信这将是一场核战争。” 日本原子弹幸存者（被称为“原爆幸存者”）的平均年龄已接近 87 岁。他们面临着向年轻一代，包括他们的子孙和支持者传递他们的证词和和平呼吁的紧迫挑战。 来自长崎的第二代原子弹幸存者中村贵子 (Takako Nakamura) 在职业生涯退休后，于 2026 年 2 月开始积极担任家庭证词发言人。 “人们被杀得无影无踪，连骨头都没有留下。这就是原子弹的真正本质，”...

title.en: The Australians spending their European summer waiting for a 15-minute warning
title.zh: 澳大利亚人正在欧洲度过夏季，等待15分钟的火情警报

summary.en: Australian aerial firefighting pilots are increasingly spending their European summers assisting local authorities in combating wildfires, often waiting for short-notice deployment.
summary.zh: 越来越多的澳大利亚空中消防飞行员在欧洲夏季帮助当地政府扑灭野火，他们常常在等待短时间通知后立即投入工作。

body.en:
While most Australians in Europe are at the beach, NSW aerial firefighting pilot Alex Pay spends his long summer days at a Greek airbase, waiting for a call to action.

"When you get a fire call, you're gonna be airborne in 15 minutes," he told SBS News.

Once in the air, Pay can spend up to 10 hours supporting local authorities in Greece's fight against wildfires, which over the past week saw two pilots killed and hundreds of thousands forced to evacuate.

Pay, 31, works for a small but growing number of Australian private aerial firefighting companies based in Western Europe during this year's fire season, which is shaping up to be the continent's worst in record.

It also comes as Australia's own looming El Niño threatens to turn up the heat on our own summer bushfire risk .

Pay is a third-generation pilot with Pay's Air Service, which is based in the NSW Hunter Region.

"I remember as a kid flying with my dad to visit my grandparents," he told SBS News.

He pilots one of 14 aircraft his company has based throughout Greece for the summer. It’s his second season in the country, and the fifth overall for his company.

They fly a variant of the Air Tractor AT-802, nicknamed the "Fire Boss" — an amphibious aircraft that scoops water into a tank, or "hopper", controlled by a computerised fire gate that can be adjusted to match exact conditions.

In Australia, there were around 130 certified firefighting aeroplane operators or individual pilots, with a further 186 helicopter operators in 2021, according to Australia's Civil Aviation Authority.

Andrew Mackay is from Ballarat-based Field Air Group, which also has planes stationed in Greece this summer supporting Pay's.

"We like to say in our industry that it's not the aircraft that put out the fires, it's the ground crew — we're merely a tool to assist them," he told SBS News.

He said pilots will often work on either side of the fire to create a "triangle or an arrowhead, so the fire comes to a point where the ground crew can then extinguish that".

Sometimes they will drop water or retardant directly onto a house under threat from a blaze.

"We spent a lot of time training and preparing scenarios that give us a good education on what we might see on the fire ground," Pay said.

On Sunday, a Greek and a Danish national were killed after two helicopters collided while fighting a fire west of Athens.

The helicopters were leased from Australian company McDermott Aviation, which said in a statement it was "deeply saddened" by the tragedy.

title.en: As allies desert FIFA boss Gianni Infantino, is there anyone ready to replace him?
title.zh: 随着盟友抛弃国际足联主席詹尼·因凡蒂诺，谁能取代他？

summary.en: FIFA President Gianni Infantino is facing significant controversy, leading to a loss of support from allies and questions about his future leadership.

body.en:
Pressure on FIFA president Gianni Infantino has intensified, with opposition emerging both within world football's governing body and from external critics over his since-abandoned proposal to open the World Cup to private investment.

Former Arsenal manager Arsene Wenger, appointed in 2019 by Infantino as FIFA's chief of global football development, said in a statement on Tuesday that "the decision to withdraw the project was absolutely necessary and beyond question".

His remarks followed hot on the heels of an extraordinary internal email to FIFA staff, seen by the Agence France-Presse (AFP) news agency, in which secretary-general Mattias Grafstrom appeared to distance himself from Infantino on the issue.

Previously seen as close to Infantino, Grafstrom describes the fiasco surrounding the plan as "a sad and reproachable series of events".

FIFA floated the plan last Tuesday, saying it could raise up to US$4.2 billion ($5.95 billion) of private investment based on a valuation of US$20 billion ($28 billion) for a new commercial subsidiary, called the FIFA Forward Enterprise (FFE), which it proposed would handle commercial rights for events such as the World Cup and Club World Cup.

By Saturday, it was dead in the water, as Infantino announced he was abandoning the plan after widespread condemnation, with European governing body UEFA having threatened to boycott all FIFA competitions, including the World Cup.

Far from calming the waters or shoring up his presidency, Infantino has been swamped with criticism of his leadership style; the previously smooth path to being re-elected unopposed for a fourth and final term next March now looks rocky.

However, re-election is a problem down the road. For now, Infantion has others to confront.

Even though he had withdrawn the scheme, UEFA issued a letter through their lawyers in the US threatening legal action over what they had scathingly described as a "shabby, backroom, opaque deal".

"You and FIFA are required to take immediate steps to identify, locate, and preserve all documents and electronically stored information described in this Notice that are in your or FIFA's possession, custody, or control," its lawyer Andrew Levander said in the letter sent last Friday and seen by AFP.

Several of UEFA's member associations — Wales, Finland, Sweden and Serbia — have withdrawn their letters of support for Infantino and the English FA is strongly rumoured to be on the verge of joining them.

summary.en: An estimated 60,000 people rushed into Spain's North African territory, causing major concerns throughout the European Union.

body.en:
Spain's interior minister headed into a tense face-off with EU counterparts on Tuesday, as the bloc sought to draw lessons from an influx of migrants into Spain's North African enclave of Ceuta in hastily arranged video talks.

The unprecedented sight of an estimated 60,000 people streaming into Ceuta from Morocco — dozens died in the attempt and almost all have since left — exposed the fault lines on migration among EU nations.

Since images first emerged of the mass arrivals, most of whom swam around a barrier separating the enclave from Morocco, the Spanish government has found itself pitted against many of its EU partners.

The bloc's interior ministers dialled in for a videoconference that could provide a chance to look for common ground — but looked equally likely to set the stage for a showdown.

While Spain moved swiftly to send migrants back from Ceuta — where it said an estimated 2,500 remained as of Monday — the government of Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez backs a more open approach to migration than most of its EU counterparts.

Countries pushing a harder line are led most vocally by Italy — whose Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has attacked Madrid's stance, and specifically a recent push to grant legal status to undocumented migrants already in the country.

Both Italy and Denmark last week advocated suspending Spain from the Schengen free-travel area over the Ceuta crisis — a notion firmly rejected by Madrid, and which in any case is legally impossible under EU rules.

In a letter to the heads of the EU's institutions Saturday, Sanchez accused fellow EU countries of having "selfish" attitudes and called for emergency talks to work on a "common response" to such incidents.

Within hours, 22 countries led by Italy, Denmark, Germany and Hungary sent a counter-letter also demanding urgent talks, but with a different goal: to continue pressing their tough stance on immigration.

In a taste of what to expect, preparatory talks among the bloc's EU ambassadors on Monday saw Spain's envoy voice "frustration" with a perceived lack of support from fellow capitals, one EU diplomat told the Agence-France Presse (AFP) news agency.

Conversely — while all assured Madrid of their "solidarity" — some member states "are asking themselves if recent policies adopted by Spain have not sent the signal that the doors are open", added the diplomat.

The EU has significantly tightened its migration rules in recent months, including by allowing member states to send failed asylum seekers to so-called "return hubs" located outside the bloc's borders.

body.en:
Japan needs to boost its military with a "sense of urgency and crisis", its defence minister said on Tuesday, as a new government assessment reiterated growing risks posed by China, North Korea, and Russia.

Japan is already beefing up military spending and security cooperation in Asia, deploying missile launchers to outer islands, moving to acquire "counter-strike" capabilities, and easing rules on weapons exports.

But Shinjiro Koizumi said in a preface to the annual defence white paper that it was "imperative that Japan further reinforce and transform its defence capabilities with a stronger sense of urgency and crisis than ever before".

In the Asia-Pacific, "not only are China and North Korea further strengthening their military capabilities, China-Russia and Russia-North Korea are also reinforcing their cooperation", he added.

The new white paper said China was "intensifying its activities" in the region around Japan, "extending beyond the so-called first island chain to the second island chain".

reflection.zh: 在一个不信任感加剧常导致军事集结的世界里，先知以赛亚提供了一个不同未来的愿景。他预见到一个国家将把武器铸成和平与生产工具，不再学习战争的时代。这提醒我们为领袖和人民祷告，使其寻求和解与相互理解的道路，而非升级军备竞赛。

verse.textEn: They will beat their swords into plowshares and their spears into pruning hooks.
verse.textZh: 他们要将刀打成犁头，把枪打成镰刀。

title.en: China Desk
title.zh: 中国观察

strap.en: Policy signals, social change, and national developments inside China.
strap.zh: 聚焦中国内部政策走向、社会变化与国家动态。

title.en: US to shut five consulates as critics fear China could fill diplomatic vacuum
title.zh: 美国将关闭五个领事馆，因批评人士担心中国可能填补外交真空

summary.en: State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: State department informs Congress of planned closures in Canada, Grenada, Japan, Indonesia and Cameroon The US state department is to shut five foreign consulates and missions across Asia, Africa, North America and the Caribbean, drawing criticism that it is leaving a diplomatic vacuum at risk of being filled by China. The US Congress has been served notice of the impending closures, which are being justified on cost grounds and follow a reassessment of the US’s bilateral relationships with a range of countries since Donald Trump returned to the White House in January 2025. Continue reading...
body.zh: 美国国务院通知国会计划关闭加拿大、格林纳达、日本、印度尼西亚和喀麦隆 美国国务院将关闭亚洲、非洲、北美和加勒比地区的五个外国领事馆和使团，此举招致批评，称此举留下的外交真空有可能被中国填补。美国国会已收到即将关闭工厂的通知，出于成本考虑，关闭工厂是合理的，并且自唐纳德·特朗普 2025 年 1 月重返白宫以来，美国对美国与一系列国家的双边关系进行了重新评估。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to leadership, wisdom, and public responsibility. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with wisdom, integrity, and service, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到领导、智慧与公共责任。Proverbs 11:14提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以智慧、正直与服事来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Democracy is at stake when foolish humans bet on machines being intelligent | Rafael Behr
title.zh: 当愚蠢的人类押注机器智能时，民主就岌岌可危 | 拉斐尔·贝尔

summary.en: The article argues that democracy is jeopardized when human leaders unwisely place their trust in artificial intelligence. It highlights the critical need for enlightened leadership, particularly from the US president, to advocate for global AI regulation, contrasting this need with current political realities.
summary.zh: 文章指出，当人类领导者不明智地将信任寄托于人工智能时，民主就会受到威胁。它强调了开明领导人（特别是美国总统）推动全球人工智能监管的迫切需求，并将其与当前的政治现实进行了对比。

body.en: We need an enlightened US president to make the case for global AI regulation. Donald Trump is the exact opposite of what is needed When I am woken by the sound of my dog whining, I understand that she is hungry and wants me to get up. When my alarm clock goes off, I don’t consider its needs. It is following an instruction to rouse me at a certain time but it doesn’t care if I stay in bed. It doesn’t try to get me up by other means. The dog, on the other hand, will go to plan B. She barks. This capacity for autonomous action was once a difference between animals and machines. AI has blurred the line . Advanced models devise their own strategies to reach a goal. The task might be defined by a human master, but the machine weighs its options for delivery. It can make its own choices. Given rules, it can break them. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我们需要一位开明的美国总统来为全球人工智能监管提供理由。唐纳德·特朗普与我们所需要的恰恰相反。当我被狗的哀鸣声吵醒时，我知道她饿了，想让我起床。当我的闹钟响起时，我不会考虑它的需求。它会按照指令在特定时间叫醒我，但它并不关心我是否留在床上。它不会试图通过其他方式让我起床。另一方面，狗会执行 B 计划。她会吠叫。这种自主行动的能力曾经是动物和机器之间的区别。人工智能已经模糊了界限。先进的模型会制定自己的策略来实现目标。该任务可能由人类主人定义，但机器会权衡其交付选项。它可以做出自己的选择。既定规则，它可能会打破它们。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence challenges us to consider the limits of human understanding and the wisdom needed to govern powerful new technologies. As we navigate this complex future, Yahweh's word reminds us not to lean solely on our own intellect or creations, but to seek a deeper, divine wisdom. True discernment comes from trusting in...
reflection.zh: 人工智能的迅速发展促使我们思考人类理解的局限性，以及管理强大新兴科技所需的智慧。当我们驾驭这个复杂的未来时，雅伟的话语提醒我们不要单单依靠自己的智力或创造物，而要寻求更深层的、来自雅伟的智慧。真正的洞察力来自于全心信靠雅伟，尤其是在面对影响社会根基的决策时。

verse.textEn: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.
verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

title.en: A moment that changed me: I found a forbidden novel – it led to a dangerous, lasting love
title.zh: 改变我的时刻：我发现了一本禁忌小说——它导致了一段危险而持久的爱情

summary.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed...
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en: Growing up in the Chinese region of Xinjiang, romance was frowned upon – as was much of my Uyghur culture. But one day, exploring a strange house, I found a gateway to both worlds Many people have a book that changes their life. For me and my wife, one book in particular changed our destinies for ever. We have been in love since we were teenagers, and today we are happily married – all because I accidentally discovered a forbidden novel in someone else’s house. It was a hot summer’s evening in 2009, in Kumul, Xinjiang. I was 16 and my father insisted I accompany him to visit a distant relative, where they would spend hours chatting about the old days and feasting as if they hadn’t eaten in years. As the well-behaved teenager I tried to be, I sat politely, nodding at their stories and pretending to absorb their “life lessons”, attempting to hide my boredom. The living room, with its small windows and bright lighting, was unbearable. Continue reading...
body.zh: 我在中国新疆地区长大，浪漫是不受欢迎的——就像我的维吾尔文化一样。但有一天，在探索一栋陌生的房子时，我发现了通往两个世界的大门许多人都有一本改变他们生活的书。对于我和我的妻子来说，有一本书永远改变了我们的命运。我们从少年时就相爱，到今天幸福地结婚了——这一切都是因为我无意中在别人家里发现了一本禁书。 2009年，新疆哈密尔一个炎热的夏夜。我当时 16 岁，父亲坚持让我陪他去拜访一位远房亲戚，他们会花上几个小时谈论过去的时光，然后大吃大喝，就好像他们已经很多年没有吃饭一样了。作为一个我努力成为的乖孩子，我礼貌地坐着，对他们的故事点头，假装吸收他们的“人生教训”，试图隐藏我的无聊。客厅的窗户很小，灯光明亮，令人难以忍受。继续阅读...

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

verse.textEn: Blessed are the peacemakers, for they will be called children of God.
verse.textZh: 使人和睦的人有福了，因为他们必称为神的儿子。

title.en: Trump administration reportedly drafting ban on Chinese datacenter components
title.zh: 据报道，特朗普政府正起草一项针对中国数据中心组件的禁令

summary.en: The Trump administration is reportedly preparing a ban on US imports of new Chinese datacenter components. This measure, being developed by the FCC, signals an effort by US authorities to address concerns related to technology and trade.
summary.zh: 据报道，特朗普政府正在起草一项禁止美国进口新型中国数据中心组件的禁令。这项由联邦通信委员会（FCC）制定的措施，表明美国当局正努力应对与技术和贸易相关的担忧。

body.en: Trump’s FCC is developing a measure to bar US imports of new models of Chinese datacenter devices, sources say The Trump administration is reportedly drafting a ban on US imports of new models of Chinese datacenter components, in the latest sign US authorities are scrambling to respond to the rapid development of AI technology in China . Four people familiar with the matter told Reuters that the Federal Communications Commission (FCC), which oversees the US ⁠telecommunications industry, is developing a measure to bar imports of new ​Chinese optical transceivers, which allow data to travel over fiber-optic cables at the speed of light within datacenters. Officials hope to publish the measure this year, according to Reuters. Continue reading...
body.zh: 消息人士称，特朗普政府的联邦通信委员会正在制定一项措施，禁止美国进口新型中国数据中心设备。 据报道，特朗普政府正在起草一项禁止美国进口新型中国数据中心组件的禁令，这是美国当局正忙于应对中国人工智能技术快速发展的最新迹象。四名知情人士告诉路透社，负责监管美国电信行业的联邦通信委员会（FCC）正在制定一项措施，禁止进口新型中国光收发器，这些光收发器允许数据在数据中心内通过光纤电缆以光速传输。据路透社报道，官员们希望今年公布这项措施。继续阅读...

reflection.en: In a world of complex technological dependencies and geopolitical tensions, nations often seek to anticipate and mitigate potential risks. Proverbs 27:12 reminds us of the wisdom in foreseeing danger and taking prudent steps to protect what is valuable. Such foresight, applied with integrity, can guide leaders in navigating intricate global challenges.
reflection.zh: 在一个技术相互依赖和地缘政治紧张复杂的世界中，各国常常寻求预见并减轻潜在风险。箴言27:12提醒我们，预见危险并采取审慎措施保护宝贵之物是智慧之举。这种以正直为基础的远见，能够指引领导者应对错综复杂的全球挑战。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: Stock market turmoil sheds stark light on the opaque AI economy
title.zh: 股市动荡揭示不透明的人工智能经济

summary.en: Investors scramble to make sense of a shock Chinese challenge to the dominance of western chipmakers, leading to a particularly volatile week in the AI economy.
summary.zh: 投资者急于理解中国对西方芯片制造商主导地位的冲击，这导致人工智能经济在上周经历了特别剧烈的波动。

body.en: Investors scramble to make sense of a shock Chinese challenge to the dominance of western chipmakers Even for the rollercoaster world of AI, last week was particularly volatile as investors scrambled to keep up with developments that threatened the dominance of the largest western chipmakers. It began with a double whammy. On Monday, the Chinese memory chipmaker CXMT floated on the Shanghai stock market, soaring by 466% in value to 3.3tn yuan (£365bn). Continue reading...
body.zh: 投资者争先恐后地理解中国对西方芯片制造商主导地位的令人震惊的挑战即使对于像过山车一样的人工智能世界来说，上周也特别动荡，因为投资者争先恐后地跟上威胁西方最大芯片制造商主导地位的发展。它开始于双重打击。周一，中国存储芯片制造商长鑫存储在上海股市上市，市值飙升 466% 至 3.3 亿元人民币（3,650 亿英镑）。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid shifts and opaque nature of the AI economy, as seen in recent market turmoil, highlight how quickly human understanding can be overwhelmed by complex systems. In moments when investors scramble to make sense of unpredictable developments, Proverbs 3:5 reminds us to lean not on our own understanding, but to trust in Yahweh with all our heart. This...
reflection.zh: 人工智能经济的快速变化和不透明性，正如近期市场动荡所显示，突显了人类理解力在复杂系统面前的局限。当投资者努力理解不可预测的发展时，箴言3:5提醒我们不要依靠自己的聪明，而要全心信赖雅伟。这鼓励我们在自身洞察力有限时，保持谦卑并依靠神的智慧。

verse.textEn: Trust in Yahweh with all your heart and lean not on your own understanding.
verse.textZh: 你要专心仰赖雅伟，不可倚靠自己的聪明。

title.en: China has banned hidden retractable car door handles. How are they dangerous – and what will Australia do?
title.zh: 中国已禁止隐藏式可伸缩汽车门把手。它们为何危险？澳大利亚会效仿吗？

summary.en: China has banned hidden retractable car door handles, citing their failure to operate during accidents and trapping passengers in burning vehicles. These handles were popularized by Tesla electric vehicles, and the move raises questions about whether other countries like Australia will follow suit.
summary.zh: 中国已禁止使用隐藏式可伸缩汽车门把手，理由是它们在事故中可能失灵，导致乘客被困在燃烧的车辆中。特斯拉电动汽车普及了这种门把手，此举引发了其他国家（如澳大利亚）是否会效仿的疑问。

body.en: The handles, which were popularised by Elon Musk’s Tesla EVs, have a record of failing and trapping passengers inside burning vehicles during deadly accidents Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Get our breaking news email , free app or daily news podcast They used to be a novelty in Australia: the futuristic, flush-mounted car door handles favoured by Elon Musk’s Tesla. However while the design – popularised with the Tesla Model S in 2012 and since adopted by other manufacturers – might look sleek, it may not be great in an emergency. Continue reading...
body.zh: 这些把手因埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 的特斯拉电动汽车而广受欢迎，但在致命事故中曾发生过故障，并将乘客困在燃烧的车辆内。 关注我们的澳大利亚新闻直播博客，了解最新动态 获取我们的突发新闻电子邮件、免费应用程序或每日新闻播客 它们曾经是澳大利亚的新奇事物：埃隆·马斯克 (Telsas) 青睐的未来派嵌入式汽车门把手。然而，虽然这种设计在 2012 年随特斯拉 Model S 流行起来，后来被其他制造商采用，但虽然看起来很时尚，但在紧急情况下可能不太好。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The ban on retractable car door handles highlights the importance of foresight in design and technology. A prudent person foresees danger and takes precautions, reminding us that innovation must always be balanced with safety and the well-being of others. This decision underscores the responsibility to protect lives by addressing foreseeable risks, even in...
reflection.zh: 对可伸缩汽车门把手的禁令突显了设计和技术中预见危险的重要性。通达人预见祸患就藏躲，提醒我们创新必须始终与安全和他人福祉相平衡。这一决定强调了通过解决可预见的风险来保护生命的责任，即使是在看似微小的设计选择中。

verse.textEn: The prudent see danger and take refuge, but the simple keep going and pay the penalty.
verse.textZh: 通达人见祸藏躲；愚蒙人前往受害。

title.en: China’s tech advances are causing chaos from Silicon Valley to the White House
title.zh: 中国的科技进步正在从硅谷到白宫引发混乱

summary.en: Recent advancements in China's artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing, and robotics technologies have caused significant disruption in global financial markets and the US tech industry.
summary.zh: 中国在人工智能、芯片制造和机器人技术方面取得的最新进展，已在全球金融市场和美国科技行业引发了显著的震荡。

body.en: New AI models, advanced robots and specialty computer chips are unsettling markets and the US tech industry Over the past month, a series of advancements in China’s artificial intelligence, chip manufacturing and robotics technologies have rattled financial markets, caused divisions among US tech moguls and left the Trump administration scrambling to respond. Silicon Valley has long pointed to China’s tech industry as a competitive threat and used its growth as rationale for why US firms should not face regulatory oversight that could slow them down. In recent weeks, however, China’s progress has pushed US tech CEOs past vague warnings and into open disagreement over how to address Chinese-made products upending their industry. Continue reading...
body.zh: 新的人工智能模型、先进机器人和专用计算机芯片令市场和美国科技行业感到不安。过去一个月，中国人工智能、芯片制造和机器人技术的一系列进步震惊了金融市场，引发了美国科技大亨之间的分歧，并让特朗普政府仓促应对。硅谷长期以来一直将中国科技行业视为竞争威胁，并以中国科技行业的增长作为美国企业不应面临可能放慢发展速度的监管监督的理由。然而，最近几周，中国的进步让美国科技公司的首席执行官不再发出含糊的警告，而是在如何解决颠覆其行业的中国制造产品问题上产生了公开分歧。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid pace of technological innovation, particularly in AI and robotics, reflects a time when knowledge is indeed increasing at an unprecedented rate. This acceleration can bring both wonder and apprehension as societies grapple with its profound implications. In such moments, we are reminded to seek wisdom beyond mere information, trusting Yahweh to...
reflection.zh: 人工智能和机器人技术等领域的快速创新步伐，正反映出知识以前所未有的速度增长的时代。这种加速既带来惊奇，也引发担忧，因为社会正在努力应对其深远影响。在这样的时刻，我们被提醒要寻求超越单纯信息的智慧，信靠雅伟引导我们穿越新的领域。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: World-renowned climber Nirmal Purja among 11 struck by avalanche on Pakistan mountain
title.zh: 世界著名登山家尼尔马尔·普尔贾等11人在巴基斯坦山脉遭遇雪崩

summary.en: World-renowned climber Nirmal Purja was among 11 mountaineers caught in a deadly avalanche on Broad Peak in Pakistan. Rescuers have found four bodies as the search continues for the team.
summary.zh: 世界著名登山家尼尔马尔·普尔贾是11名在巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰遭遇致命雪崩的登山者之一。救援人员已找到四具遗体，搜寻工作仍在进行中。

body.en: Rescuers say four bodies found in search for team caught in Broad Peak avalanche, after trackers showed rapid descent The world-renowned Nepali mountaineer Nirmal Purja – a former British special forces member – is among 11 climbers caught in a deadly avalanche on Pakistan’s Broad Peak. The Alpine Club of Pakistan said “seven climbers have been spotted via aerial drone footage” adding that “their identities and condition cannot yet be verified”. Continue reading...
body.zh: 救援人员称，在追踪器显示快速下降后，在寻找布洛阿特峰雪崩中陷入雪崩的登山队时，发现了四具尸体。世界著名的尼泊尔登山家尼尔马尔·普贾（Nirmal Purja）是一名前英国特种部队成员，他是巴基斯坦布洛阿特峰遭遇雪崩的 11 名登山者之一。巴基斯坦高山俱乐部表示，“通过无人机航拍发现了七名登山者”，并补充说“他们的身份和状况尚未得到证实”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The tragic news of climbers caught in an avalanche reminds us of life's fragility and the suddenness of loss. In moments of profound grief and pain, we hold onto the promise that one day Yahweh will wipe away every tear. This hope assures us that suffering, mourning, and death will ultimately pass away.
reflection.zh: 登山者遭遇雪崩的悲剧性新闻提醒我们生命的脆弱和失去的突然。在极度悲伤和痛苦的时刻，我们紧紧抓住雅伟有一天将擦去我们所有眼泪的应许。这个盼望向我们保证，苦难、哀伤和死亡终将过去。

verse.textEn: He will wipe every tear from their eyes. There will be no more death or mourning or crying or pain.
verse.textZh: 神要擦去他们一切的眼泪；不再有死亡，也不再有悲哀、哭号、疼痛。

title.en: From petitions to memes: How students made dissent visible
title.zh: 从请愿到网络迷因：学生如何让异议显现

summary.en: Student movements throughout history, from imperial China to modern India, have consistently found new ways to express dissent and challenge established authority, adapting their methods to contemporary tools and symbols.
summary.zh: 从中国古代到当今印度，学生运动不断调整其工具和象征，以挑战权威，使异议得以显现。

body.en:
From imperial China to present-day India, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols of their age to challenge authority.

On July 22, 2026, in rainy Mumbai, India , a casually dressed young woman stepped in front of a slow-moving police van carrying detained students. She placed her palm on the hood, forcing the vehicle to stop.

Mobile phones captured the moment from every angle. She too, raised her own phone and recorded the encounter. Within hours, the clip spread across India and beyond.

It became one of the defining visuals of the Cockroach Janta Party protests, a movement in which students demanded transparency and accountability, following leaks in India's medical entrance exams.

But the power of the moment lay not only in what she did, but in how quickly it was seen. A single gesture, a young woman confronting authority , became a symbol shared across millions of screens.

While the clip belongs to a generation raised on social media, the impulse behind it is much older.

From court petitions and revolutionary posters to photographs, umbrellas and memes, student movements have repeatedly adapted the tools and symbols available to them, turning them into vehicles for dissent.

Long before television or social media carried dissent across borders, students still found ways to make their grievances heard.

In Eastern Han China, for instance, scholars at the Imperial Academy (Taixue) aligned with reform-minded officials in opposing powerful eunuchs at court, whom many viewed as corrupt and politically overbearing.

They voiced their objections through public criticism, political networks and petitions.

In an era when political communication moved through official channels, petitions were among the established ways of bringing grievances before the throne. Written in formal language and delivered through the bureaucracy, they carried student concerns directly into the state's communication system.

In Paris in 1968, students challenged university authorities and a conservative postwar social order. As demonstrations spread across the French capital and drew in workers, one of the movement's most enduring contributions emerged from a basement workshop at the Ecole des Beaux-Arts.

The Atelier Populaire ("People's Workshop") printed thousands of posters during the protests, many of them overnight. Their bold graphics, silhouettes and slogans became the visual language of the movement. Produced collectively, many carried no individual author's name, helping transform protest into a shared public voice.

The posters and their messages could appear in dozens of places overnight, giving the protest a wide local visual presence.

Protests also became more impactful when images could be transmitted across borders.

title.en: US-China AI rivalry heats up as Chinese models gain ground
title.zh: 中美人工智能竞争加剧，中国模型迎头赶上

summary.en: China's AI platforms are rapidly advancing, narrowing the gap with US technology. This progress has led to renewed threats from the Trump administration, alongside accusations of intellectual property theft, raising concerns about escalating tensions between the two nations.
summary.zh: 中国的人工智能平台正迅速缩小与美国同行的差距。这一进展引发了特朗普政府新的威胁，并伴随着知识产权盗窃的指控，令人担忧两国之间的紧张关系可能升级。

body.en:
China's AI platforms are rapidly closing the gap with their US counterparts, prompting fresh threats from the Trump administration. With accusations of intellectual property theft, could tensions boil over?

In what seems like the blink of an eye,  China has gone from being up to five years behind the United States in top-tier artificial intelligence (AI) to lagging by just a few months.

While US players, including Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT , have spent hundreds of billions of dollars to push the frontier of AI, China has pursued a very different path .

Faced with US curbs on high-end chips that help AI to do its most advanced thinking, Chinese tech firms have prioritized dozens of open-source AI models built on "good enough"  technology .

These platforms, including DeepSeek, Alibaba's Qwen and Xiaomi's MiMo, are now widely deployed across Chinese businesses, government services and consumer devices.

In the latest sign of the gap closing, Chinese startup Moonshot AI last week unveiled Kimi K3, a model that rivals one of the most advanced AI models — Anthropic's Claude Fable 5 — on key benchmarks.

In some tests, Kimi K3 matches or even surpasses Claude with far less computing power and at a fraction of the cost. 

Global technology specialist Alvin W. Graylin thinks Kimi K3's arrival turns high-end AI from an expensive luxury into something practical and affordable.

"For 98% of customers, the 1 to 2% difference [in knowledge] isn't worth paying 10 to 20 times more."

China's latest advance has already drawn a strong reaction from Washington, with US President Donald Trump now threatening to block US access to Chinese AI models.

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, meanwhile, warned earlier this week that the US could sanction Chinese models over alleged intellectual property (IP) theft.

Anthropic  and OpenAI have accused Chinese labs of using their models to train their own systems, a process known as distilling.

While distilling is a common practice by AI labs worldwide to a limited extent, the companies say their models have been bombarded with queries to harvest advanced reasoning. The White House warned in April that China was doing it on an "industrial scale."

Beijing has hit back, rejecting the accusations as baseless and calling US threats of sanctions and model bans "technological bullying" to contain China's rise.

Giulia Neaher, a research analyst at the Strategic Foresight Hub at the Washington-based Stimson Center think tank, downplayed the role of distilling in Kimi's progress.

title.en: High Court finds secret recording can be used as evidence in domestic violence case
title.zh: 高庭裁定秘密录音可作为家庭暴力案件证据

summary.en: Recordings of private conversations are usually illegal. The High Court allowed it to be used as evidence in this case.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Victim-survivors of domestic violence might now be able to use secret recordings of admissions of abuse to seek safety after a major High Court decision.

Australia's highest court on Wednesday dismissed an appeal from a man convicted of raping his wife while she slept on two occasions.

He had argued a recording of him admitting to the first rape was obtained illegally.

While most recordings of private conversations are illegal , the High Court found the recording was allowed and able to be used as evidence because it was necessary to protect the victim's "bodily autonomy and integrity".

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

"The covert recording was the reminder to the complainant, by replaying it to herself, to avoid being exposed to the real risk of being raped," the court said in its unanimous judgment.

"The interest of a person in not being raped is an interest deserving of the very strongest protection."

The man, known by the pseudonym Potter, was found guilty in South Australia of raping his sleeping wife on two occasions while the jury could not reach a verdict on two further counts.

A month before the last rape, his wife recorded a conversation on her phone where she confronted Potter about the attacks, and he admitted to doing them.

The woman gave evidence that she made the recording to "convince myself never to go back to him no matter what happened".

Heather Douglas is a legal expert and professor at Melbourne Law School. She said protecting the rights of victim-survivors to record — and use as evidence — confessions of abuse inflicted on them is a major milestone for domestic violence law in Australia.

"The decision is important as it explicitly recognises that a lawful interest includes a right of bodily autonomy and integrity in the context of recordings," Douglas said.

The influence of the High Court's decision could extend beyond criminal cases, potentially allowing for similar recordings to be used in protection applications, according to Douglas.

However, it remains to be seen how far courts will allow secret recordings to be used to as evidence against less obvious forms of abuse.

Douglas believes, "much of the most damaging domestic and family violence is non-physical, such as coercive control, and this form of abuse impacts autonomy".

title.en: Health insurance rebates are changing for some Australians. Here's what to expect
title.zh: 对于一些澳大利亚人来说，健康保险回扣正在发生变化。这是值得期待的

summary.en: Will a new policy change push people to drop their private health insurance coverage?
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及对脆弱群体的怜悯。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Since the federal government announced earlier this year it would scrap the higher private health insurance rebate for people aged 65 and over, opponents have come out in force.

Private Healthcare Australia, the insurers’ peak body, says the government’s own modelling of about 44,000 older Australians dropping their cover due to the resulting higher premiums is a "significant underestimate”.

Three state health ministers have warned the change would push more people into their strained public hospitals.

So how many people would really drop their cover as a result of this policy change?

Our new research , designed specifically to test this question, gives some clues. In a nutshell, the sky won’t fall in.

Your trusted source for staying up-to-date with the world around you. Get free daily news updates and analysis, straight to your inbox.

Right now, the private health insurance rebate depends on both income and age. Someone 65 or over gets a bigger government rebate on their premium than someone under 65 on the same income. This rebate increases further for those aged 70 and over.

From April 2027, the government proposes removing that age-based bonus. So the rebate would be equal for everyone on the same income, regardless of age.

The government argues this fixes a subsidy that’s inequitable and poorly targeted, so will improve intergenerational equity.

Its own modelling predicts the vast majority of affected policyholders — about 99 per cent — would keep their cover. This means about 44,000 would drop it.

This agrees with our earlier research showing most older Australians don’t need a bigger rebate to keep their insurance.

But last week, Private Healthcare Australia released polling of more than 1,500 people showing 39 per cent of insured older Australians say they’d be more likely to drop their cover.

Based on the number of privately insured Australians aged 65 and over, that would mean about one million people, considerably more than the government’s predictions.

Our new research looks at the impacts of the government’s proposal. We used a decade of tax data, taking into account how the rebate had shifted over time.

What makes our research unique is that we separated out the impact of Australia’s two big private health insurance levers — the rebate and the Medicare Levy Surcharge tax penalty. That means we could focus on the impact of scrapping the extra health insurance rebates for the over 65s without muddying the waters.

body.en:
Getting the help you need for a winter illness could be simpler than spending hours waiting to be seen in a busy hospital emergency room.

That's the message the government is sending this flu season, a time when experts say hospitals tend to be the busiest, and wait times blow out.

While managing cold and flu cases is a national health concern, one state is taking a particularly strong stance, urging people to avoid the emergency room unless their lives are at risk.

On Monday, just under 10,000 people presented to emergency departments in Sydney, which the NSW health minister has described as the "biggest ever recorded winter day in history".

Professor Paul Griffin from the University of Queensland School of Medicine told SBS News that while numbers will vary between states, this time of year is often busy nationwide.

Across Australia, Griffin said healthcare services were seeing presentations of flu and RSV (respiratory syncytial virus), as well as an increase in COVID-19 cases.

While these can be concerning conditions, an emergency room will always prioritise the most severe health conditions first, Griffin explained.

"If you don't need to go to your emergency department, it does free up valuable resources for them to be able to deal with more emerging cases," he said.

"There are a number of viable options for people that have conditions that are a little bit less urgent, and that's why we want people to make sure that they understand where the best place for them to go really is."

The Australian government has outlined three broad categories of care — routine, urgent and emergency — each with varying symptom severity, encompassing flu symptoms as well as broader conditions.

Most health issues can be addressed through routine care, which for many people means their GP.

Griffin said GPs are not only a good touchpoint for receiving care when sick but can also help you prepare a plan ahead of potential illness.

They can provide health checks, vaccinations and offer family and individual health advice.

"If it's something that you're not feeling needs urgent attention, then your GP is often the best place to start to get the care that you need," Griffin said.

If you start experiencing symptoms like chest pain or feel like a respiratory illness is worsening, you may want to consider going to an urgent care clinic (UCC) or the hospital.

"If you're breathing okay, even drinking okay, not systemically unwell, your GP is a really good place to start. If any of those things aren't the case, then I'd have a very low threshold for presenting to hospital," Griffin said.

body.en:
It’s perhaps inevitable that in a large family there might be one member who is a bit of a wild card.

It’s more problematic when that family has a distinctive surname and one is a public figure.

Dominic Perrottet has 12 siblings – and his younger brother Jean-Claude Perrottet has an uncanny ability to attract headlines.

On Wednesday, Jean-Claude was the star witness at the Independent Commission against Corruption . It is investigating allegations that illegal donations were used to fund branch stacking within the NSW Liberal party by a shadowy organisation known as the Reformers, of which Jean-Claude was a key figure.

In 2017 Jean-Claude, then aged 20, was found not guilty of rape in the NSW district court.

The charges stemmed from an alcohol-charged incident with a 19-year old woman following an end-of-year formal at St John’s College, Sydney University in 2015. The jury took less than two hours to find Perrottet not guilty.

Rape cases sometimes get reported in the normal course, but because Dominic was then the youthful NSW treasurer in the Berejiklian government and the safety of women on campus was a subject of live public debate, it was regarded as highly newsworthy.

By 2018, Jean-Claude Perrottet was doing a commerce degree at the University of NSW and had found employment with conservative Catholic parliamentarians. First it was in Damien Tudehope’s electorate office, then with upper house MP David Clarke, then in 2019, back to Tudehope in his ministerial office.

He might have been a mere 21-year-old staffer, but Jean-Claude still made headlines.

In 2019, the Sydney Morning Herald published articles about an alleged concerted effort by facets of the Liberal party’s hard right to undermine sitting members in several safe state and federal seats in Sydney’s north-west.

The stories named Jean-Claude and fellow staffer Christian Ellis who were both employed at the time by Tudehope, then the minister for small business.

That was the first time we heard of the NSW Reformers, a conservative group of Catholics alleged to be behind the stacking.

Despite trying to operate covertly, the Reformers have refused to fade into obscurity.

In 2022 Liberal state MP Ray Williams, one of the Reformers’ targets, used a late night speech in parliament to raise allegations about the Reformers’ activities.

This must have been challenging for Dominic Perrottet. He would have known that, at the very least, Icac would likely question his little brother.

But these were serious allegations raised by one of his own team, involving attempts to dislodge the Hills shire council and a developer, Jean Nassif, giving the Reformers “significant funds”.

The matter ended up in a parliamentary inquiry, just months before the 2023 election.

title.en: Kmart’s $89 glasses can record what you see. But what happens next?
title.zh: Kmart的89澳元眼镜能记录你所见。但接下来会发生什么？

summary.en: Experts note a global surge in camera and smart glasses, but warn that regulating and enforcing rules for this wearable technology presents significant complexities.
summary.zh: 专家指出，全球范围内相机和智能眼镜等可穿戴技术正在迅速普及，但对其进行监管和执法却面临着更为复杂的挑战。

body.en:
Kmart recently launched a new accessory — dubbed Camera Glasses — which it said blends stylish eyewear with built-in camera technology.

At a glance, the black-framed spectacles from Kmart's in-house brand Anko look like any ordinary pair of glasses. But by Monday 3 August, there were reports the product was sold out online.

At $89, the glasses provide a low-cost alternative to the smart glasses designed by glasses company Ray-Ban and Facebook owners Meta, which start at $337. The latest generation of this technology costs more than $700.

A recent promotional video for Ray-Ban Meta AI glasses, featuring celebrity Kylie Jenner, showcased its features. Those include an ultra-HD camera, discreet open-ear Bluetooth speakers, and translation technology.

In July, Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg said people who don't wear smart glasses in the future will be at a "pretty significant cognitive disadvantage".

There are similar products available or in development by the companies Samsung, Rokid, Even Realities, Solos and XREAL.

Milica Stilinovic is a postdoctoral research associate for the Governing Immersive Tech Project at the University of Sydney. She told SBS News that "a lot of flak has been driven towards Meta currently because they are market leaders".

But she said: "If the price is cheaper ... if you're not paying at the bridge, you may pay at the toll.

"We still need to ask ourselves, this data that we're essentially generating for these companies; how is it being handled, by whom and at what cost?"

Stilinovic also said wearable technology, regardless of its price point, raises complex questions around privacy and security.

Depending on the product, they may have AI-enabled programs embedded, which analyse human behaviours including eye movements, head tracking and voice patterns.

"They are picking up data of where you're walking around, the space that you're in, what you're doing at particular times ... even to the extent of knowing the map out of your home," Stilinovic said.

Facial recognition technology is not active in most smart glasses on the market.

However, in 2024, students from Harvard University combined smart glasses, facial search engines, AI language tools and public databases to test surveillance capabilities. They found information including a person's home address, name and phone number — just by looking at them.

Fareed Kaviani is a research fellow at the Emerging Technologies Research Lab at Monash University. In 2024, he co-authored a paper examining social perceptions of smart glasses use in Australia.

title.en: The Australians spending their European summer waiting for a 15-minute warning
title.zh: 澳大利亚人正在欧洲度过夏季，等待15分钟的火情警报

summary.en: Australian aerial firefighting pilots are increasingly spending their European summers assisting local authorities in combating wildfires, often waiting for short-notice deployment.
summary.zh: 越来越多的澳大利亚空中消防飞行员在欧洲夏季帮助当地政府扑灭野火，他们常常在等待短时间通知后立即投入工作。

body.en:
While most Australians in Europe are at the beach, NSW aerial firefighting pilot Alex Pay spends his long summer days at a Greek airbase, waiting for a call to action.

"When you get a fire call, you're gonna be airborne in 15 minutes," he told SBS News.

Once in the air, Pay can spend up to 10 hours supporting local authorities in Greece's fight against wildfires, which over the past week saw two pilots killed and hundreds of thousands forced to evacuate.

Pay, 31, works for a small but growing number of Australian private aerial firefighting companies based in Western Europe during this year's fire season, which is shaping up to be the continent's worst in record.

It also comes as Australia's own looming El Niño threatens to turn up the heat on our own summer bushfire risk .

Pay is a third-generation pilot with Pay's Air Service, which is based in the NSW Hunter Region.

"I remember as a kid flying with my dad to visit my grandparents," he told SBS News.

He pilots one of 14 aircraft his company has based throughout Greece for the summer. It’s his second season in the country, and the fifth overall for his company.

They fly a variant of the Air Tractor AT-802, nicknamed the "Fire Boss" — an amphibious aircraft that scoops water into a tank, or "hopper", controlled by a computerised fire gate that can be adjusted to match exact conditions.

In Australia, there were around 130 certified firefighting aeroplane operators or individual pilots, with a further 186 helicopter operators in 2021, according to Australia's Civil Aviation Authority.

Andrew Mackay is from Ballarat-based Field Air Group, which also has planes stationed in Greece this summer supporting Pay's.

"We like to say in our industry that it's not the aircraft that put out the fires, it's the ground crew — we're merely a tool to assist them," he told SBS News.

He said pilots will often work on either side of the fire to create a "triangle or an arrowhead, so the fire comes to a point where the ground crew can then extinguish that".

Sometimes they will drop water or retardant directly onto a house under threat from a blaze.

"We spent a lot of time training and preparing scenarios that give us a good education on what we might see on the fire ground," Pay said.

On Sunday, a Greek and a Danish national were killed after two helicopters collided while fighting a fire west of Athens.

The helicopters were leased from Australian company McDermott Aviation, which said in a statement it was "deeply saddened" by the tragedy.
